newsitem.title: USA: Container leaks force New Orleans canal closing.
newsitem.headline: Container leaks force New Orleans canal closing.

text.p: The Industrial Canal remained closed Monday as authorities tried to off-load several damaged containers leaking toxic chemicals, the Coast Guard reported.
The canal, connecting the Mississippi River to the Mississippi River Gulf Outlet and Lake Pontchartrain, is considered a major industrial link for barge traffic.
The Coast Guard said Monday morning that more than two dozen barges and tugs were backed up waiting to enter the canal, which was not expected to reopen before Monday night.

The canal was closed Saturday after the barge Ponce Trader, owned by Pacific Marine Leasing of Portland, Ore., arrived from Houston with damaged containers, some of which were leaking unknown chemicals, the Coast Guard said.

One container collapsed late Friday, dumping 27 containers into the Gulf of Mexico during rough weather, according to the Coast Guard Marine Safety Office at Morgan City, La. By Monday, six of the lost containers were under tow and the location of the others unknown.
None of the lost containers was believed to be carrying hazardous materials, and one contained a car. The specific destinations of the containers was not known.
Although operations along a one-mile stretch of the canal were shut down, no residential areas have been affected, the Coast Guard said.

Eleven of the 31 damaged containers on board contained hazardous chemicals, including toluene diisocynate, vinyl acetate, dichloromethane, xylene, polyehtulene polamine, acetate acid and alcohols, the Coast Guard said.
